:::{#sol-prac-exp-mle-ci}

An [approximate](inference.qmd#def-approximate-ci) 95% CI for $\pmean$ is:

$$
\hat\pmean_{ML} \pm 1.96 \times \frac{\rvarbar}{\sqrt{n}}
= \rvarbar \pm \frac{1.96\rvarbar}{\sqrt{n}}
$$

Note: the exponential distribution has $\Varf{X} = \pmean^2$,
so $\SE{\hat\pmean_{ML}} = \pmean/\sqrt{n}$,
which is estimated by $\rvarbar/\sqrt{n}$.
More generally,
the standard error of a sample mean is $\SD{X}/\sqrt{n}$;
here the standard error reduces to $\pmean/\sqrt{n}$
because $\SD{X} = \pmean$ for the exponential distribution.

:::
